source: derived from the clause 3.2 segment header layout
note: LTP segment headers. RFC 5326 clause 3.1 defines the header as a single control octet (four-bit version, four-bit segment type), then the session ID as two SDNVs, then the Extensions field. CCSDS 734.1-B-1 adopts RFC 5326, so the clause numbers here are the RFC's. The header is variable length because the session ID is SDNV-encoded, which is what the boundary-crossing vector exists to catch.

encode.name: red-data-segment-single-octet-session
encode.note: Segment type 0 with engine ID 1 and session number 1, no extensions. Control octet = version 0<<4 | type 0 = 0x00; the two SDNVs are each a single octet 0x01; the extension counts octet is 0x00.

encode.name: wider-session-identifiers
encode.note: Engine ID 0x2a fits one SDNV octet but session number 0x1234 needs two: 0xa4 0x34. So the header is five octets, not four. This is the vector that catches a decoder assuming a fixed header size.

encode.name: engine-id-crossing-the-sdnv-boundary
encode.note: Engine ID 128 is the first value needing two SDNV octets (0x81 0x00), so the session number that follows shifts by one. A decoder that read the session number at a fixed offset would read 0x00 here instead of 1.

encode.name: report-segment-type
encode.note: Segment type 8 is a report segment, per the type code table in clause 3.1.2. Control octet = version 0<<4 | 8 = 0x08. The type occupies the low nibble, so a value above 15 has no representation.

encode.name: cancel-from-block-sender-segment-type
encode.note: Segment type 12 is a cancel segment from the block sender, per the type code table in clause 3.1.2. Control octet = 0<<4 | 12 = 0x0c. Types 8 and 12 are both control segments and differ only in the low nibble, which is why they are pinned as a pair.

decode.name: red-data-segment-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of red-data-segment-single-octet-session. A decoder must report how many octets the header consumed, because the segment content starts there and the header is variable length.

decode.name: wider-session-identifiers-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of wider-session-identifiers: five octets consumed, not four.

reject.name: version-not-zero
reject.note: Only LTP version 0 is defined. Control octet 0x10 declares version 1, which a decoder must refuse rather than misparse as a segment type.

reject.name: header-ends-inside-the-session-id
reject.note: The engine ID SDNV sets its continuation bit but the data ends, so the session ID never completes. A decoder must not get past octet 2: the engine ID SDNV sets its continuation bit and the octets run out.

reject.name: extension-count-octet-missing
reject.note: Both session SDNVs are present but the extension counts octet that must follow them is not. A decoder must not get past octet 3: both SDNVs read cleanly; the extension count octet is absent.
